claims.text: The initial material is an as-deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type high-entropy alloy in ribbon form.
The initial alloy has a single-phase hexagonal structure.
The as-deposited ribbon has relatively large grains.
Cryogenic ball milling followed by re-compaction can produce a uniformly nanocrystalline ribbon with grain sizes below 100 nm while preserving ribbon geometry.
Nanocrystalline grain refinement increases grain-boundary density.
The increased grain-boundary density supplies heterogeneous nucleation sites for the magnetostructural transition.
Grain-boundary nucleation sites lower local energy barriers for the magnetostructural transition.
Lower transformation barriers make the magnetostructural transformation more gradual and reversible.
Nanocrystalline samples will show a broader and less abrupt magnetocaloric transition than the as-deposited baseline.
Nanocrystalline samples will exhibit less hysteresis than the as-deposited baseline during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
The nanostructure enhances heat transfer through increased interfacial area.
Nanocrystalline samples will maintain or improve rapid heat-exchange performance relative to the as-deposited ribbons.
The as-deposited alloy undergoes a sharp, first-order magnetostructural transition with significant hysteresis.
The as-deposited alloy has limited heat-exchange efficiency because of bulk morphology and larger grain size.
The predicted effects are limited to samples with grain sizes below 100 nm that retain ribbon geometry and do not develop unwanted secondary phases.
TEM and EBSD can be used to compare grain-size distributions and grain-boundary density between processed and control samples.
Failure to obtain both a statistically significant hysteresis reduction and a broader, smoother transition in the nanocrystalline samples would falsify the proposed grain-boundary mechanism.

contradictions.description: The initial material is explicitly described as a ribbon, and the intervention is said to preserve its high surface-to-volume ratio, but the baseline attributes limited heat exchange to the initial material's bulk morphology. These descriptions of the baseline geometry are inconsistent.
